fetched_sources.title: PM projector webhook, reconciliation and hot-list substrate
fetched_sources.evidence: Bounded HMAC-SHA256 verification, delivery GUID idempotency, configured webhook event set, repo/stream reconciliation cursors, append-only disposable projector hot ledger with high-water paging and monotone ACK protocol, and read-only queue-view over exported task JSON plus hot list.
fetched_sources.limitations: Projector explicitly is disposable projection glue and does not write back. Its HMAC/delivery dedupe is not canonical Fleet command acceptance; the hot ACK protocol checks monotonicity/high-water but cannot prove consumer-side durability; hot ledger is not authoritative Fleet journal/outbox or complete per-resource activity/attribution; queue-view does not fetch the live broker. README notes deleted comments/overwritten historical records no longer returned by GitHub cannot be reconstructed. Source/test proof only, no deployment proof.

fetched_sources.title: Pattern: Transactional outbox
fetched_sources.evidence: Outbox row written in same DB transaction as aggregate mutation; relay sends later; relay can publish more than once if it crashes after publish before recording, so consumer idempotency is required. Notes ordering and 2PC tradeoffs.
fetched_sources.limitations: General architecture pattern; not Fleet implementation evidence.

fetched_sources.title: GitHub REST API: Pull requests; Issue comments; Pagination
fetched_sources.evidence: Merge endpoint accepts expected head SHA and returns 409 for mismatch; async merge can return 202 and distinguish accepted/enqueued from merged. Issue comments expose stable IDs, updated_at, create POST and update PATCH by ID; list comments uses ascending IDs, `since` by last updated, paginated results. Pagination uses Link next URLs; endpoint caps include 250 PR commits and 3000 PR files.
fetched_sources.limitations: Docs do not document an idempotency key or conditional CAS for issue-comment create/update in those endpoint contracts. This is a bounded claim about reviewed endpoints, not all GitHub API surfaces. Actual integration permissions/API version/branch policy require live contract tests.

fetched_sources.title: Kubernetes Controllers; Leases
fetched_sources.evidence: Controllers are loops that observe current and desired state and make/request changes toward desired; separate controllers handle distinct aspects and failures. Kubernetes Lease objects support heartbeats and leader election; holder identity/duration/renew time are coordination data.
fetched_sources.limitations: Analogy/reference architecture; Kubernetes API guarantees do not transfer to Fleet or GitHub.

fetched_sources.title: Temporal Workflow Execution overview
fetched_sources.evidence: Workflow execution is durable/recoverable via persisted event history and deterministic replay; external work is performed as Activities; workflow identity/history and execution chains are explicit. Document warns Memo metadata is not critical workflow state and can be eventually consistent.
fetched_sources.limitations: Explains Temporal's platform, not proof of Fleet need or adoption cost. Temporal activity effects still require operation-specific idempotency/reconciliation.

fetched_sources.title: SQLite Transaction Control Syntax; Isolation in SQLite
fetched_sources.evidence: SQLite permits one simultaneous writer; BEGIN IMMEDIATE obtains write transaction early; busy conflicts possible. WAL permits concurrent readers/writer with snapshot isolation; readers don't see newer commits during a transaction. Writes are serialized.
fetched_sources.limitations: Platform-specific comparator only. Fleet's actual DB/libSQL/Turso transaction and clock behavior are not established by these sources.
